newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble firms as T-bill trade captures funds.
newsitem.headline: Rouble firms as T-bill trade captures funds.

text.p: The rouble firmed in active trading on Thursday as banks closed long positions after funds failed to return to the markets from Wednesday's Treasury bill auction, dealers said.
The central bank yesterday auctioned 7.50 trillion roubles of six-month T-bills and sold 3.50 trillion roubles of an additional tranche of OFZ interest-bearing bonds.

"Banks preferred to keep the money that they did not invest yesterday on the T-bill market and not to buy dollars, contrary to what they usually do," Aljba Alliance Bank chief dealer Dmitry Slobodnik said.
"This is why rouble/dollar rates and overnight credit rates have risen -- banks need to close short (dollar) positions."
Another dealer said trading had started at lower rouble rates since the market was expecting roubles from the government bond market.
But a return of roubles into the markets was nowhere in sight, as banks actively bought all issues of T-bills and OFZ bonds.
Overnight rouble credits yielded 90-130 percent, compared with Wednesday's late 80-95 percent.

Roubles for today settlement were quoted at 5,363-66 per dollar, compared with an early 5,373-76. They were also quoted at 5,373-76 late yesterday. Tomorrow roubles firmed to 5,373-76 per dollar from yesterday's late 5,378-81.
The central bank said it had set 5,347/5,387 as its bid and offer rates against the dollar on Thursday.
Dealers said they expected the rouble to ease ahead of the weekend as investing in roubles at these credit rates for three days was not attractive.
